title: Content Providers
objectives: Explain what a ContentProvider exposes and why
Read data via a content URI and resolver
Know when you actually need one

sections.markdown: A ContentProvider exposes structured app data to other apps (or components) through a content:// URI, with a uniform CRUD interface and per-URI permissions.

sections.code:
// Read contacts via the system ContentProvider
val cursor = contentResolver.query(
  ContactsContract.Contacts.CONTENT_URI,
  null, null, null, null)

sections.markdown: You need a ContentProvider mainly when **sharing data across apps** (or to feed system features like search suggestions, widgets, or sync adapters). For purely in-app storage, use Room directly.
FileProvider is a special ContentProvider that grants temporary, secure access to files via content URIs — required to share files with other apps since Android 7 (no more file:// URIs).
Don't build a ContentProvider just to abstract your own database — that's over-engineering. Reach for one when cross-app access or a platform integration genuinely requires it.

flashcards.back: Structured data to other apps/components via content:// URIs with CRUD + permissions.
